builtin_classes.description: This is the built-in string Variant type (and the one used by GDScript). Strings may contain any number of Unicode characters, and expose methods useful for manipulating and generating strings. Strings are reference-counted and use a copy-on-write approach (every modification to a string returns a new [String]), so passing them around is cheap in resources.

methods.description: Performs a case-sensitive comparison to another string. Returns [code]-1[/code] if less than, [code]1[/code] if greater than, or [code]0[/code] if equal. "Less than" and "greater than" are determined by the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Unicode_characters]Unicode code points[/url] of each string, which roughly matches the alphabetical order.
methods.name: casecmp_to

methods.description: Performs a [b]case-insensitive[/b] comparison to another string. Returns [code]-1[/code] if less than, [code]1[/code] if greater than, or [code]0[/code] if equal. "Less than" or "greater than" are determined by the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Unicode_characters]Unicode code points[/url] of each string, which roughly matches the alphabetical order. Internally, lowercase characters are converted to uppercase for the comparison.
methods.name: nocasecmp_to

methods.description: Performs a [b]case-sensitive[/b], [i]natural order[/i] comparison to another string. Returns [code]-1[/code] if less than, [code]1[/code] if greater than, or [code]0[/code] if equal. "Less than" or "greater than" are determined by the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Unicode_characters]Unicode code points[/url] of each string, which roughly matches the alphabetical order.
methods.name: naturalcasecmp_to

methods.description: Performs a [b]case-insensitive[/b], [i]natural order[/i] comparison to another string. Returns [code]-1[/code] if less than, [code]1[/code] if greater than, or [code]0[/code] if equal. "Less than" or "greater than" are determined by the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Unicode_characters]Unicode code points[/url] of each string, which roughly matches the alphabetical order. Internally, lowercase characters are converted to uppercase for the comparison.
methods.name: naturalnocasecmp_to

methods.description: Like [method naturalcasecmp_to] but prioritizes strings that begin with periods ([code].[/code]) and underscores ([code]_[/code]) before any other character. Useful when sorting folders or file names.
methods.name: filecasecmp_to

methods.description: Like [method naturalnocasecmp_to] but prioritizes strings that begin with periods ([code].[/code]) and underscores ([code]_[/code]) before any other character. Useful when sorting folders or file names.
methods.name: filenocasecmp_to

methods.description: Returns the number of characters in the string. Empty strings ([code]""[/code]) always return [code]0[/code]. See also [method is_empty].
methods.name: length

methods.description: Returns part of the string from the position [param from] with length [param len]. If [param len] is [code]-1[/code] (as by default), returns the rest of the string starting from the given position.
methods.name: substr

methods.description: Splits the string using a [param delimiter] and returns the substring at index [param slice]. Returns the original string if [param delimiter] does not occur in the string. Returns an empty string if the [param slice] does not exist.
methods.name: get_slice

methods.description: Splits the string using a Unicode character with code [param delimiter] and returns the substring at index [param slice]. Returns an empty string if the [param slice] does not exist.
methods.name: get_slicec

methods.description: Returns the total number of slices when the string is split with the given [param delimiter] (see [method split]).
methods.name: get_slice_count

methods.description: Returns the index of the [b]first[/b] occurrence of [param what] in this string, or [code]-1[/code] if there are none. The search's start can be specified with [param from], continuing to the end of the string.
methods.name: find

methods.description: Returns the index of the [b]first[/b] [b]case-insensitive[/b] occurrence of [param what] in this string, or [code]-1[/code] if there are none. The starting search index can be specified with [param from], continuing to the end of the string.
methods.name: findn

methods.description: Returns the number of occurrences of the substring [param what] between [param from] and [param to] positions. If [param to] is 0, the search continues until the end of the string.
methods.name: count

methods.description: Returns the number of occurrences of the substring [param what] between [param from] and [param to] positions, [b]ignoring case[/b]. If [param to] is 0, the search continues until the end of the string.
methods.name: countn

methods.description: Returns the index of the [b]last[/b] occurrence of [param what] in this string, or [code]-1[/code] if there are none. The search's start can be specified with [param from], continuing to the beginning of the string. This method is the reverse of [method find].
methods.name: rfind

methods.description: Returns the index of the [b]last[/b] [b]case-insensitive[/b] occurrence of [param what] in this string, or [code]-1[/code] if there are none. The starting search index can be specified with [param from], continuing to the beginning of the string. This method is the reverse of [method findn].
methods.name: rfindn

methods.description: Does a simple expression match (also called "glob" or "globbing"), where [code]*[/code] matches zero or more arbitrary characters and [code]?[/code] matches any single character except a period ([code].[/code]). An empty string or empty expression always evaluates to [code]false[/code].
methods.name: match

methods.description: Does a simple [b]case-insensitive[/b] expression match, where [code]*[/code] matches zero or more arbitrary characters and [code]?[/code] matches any single character except a period ([code].[/code]). An empty string or empty expression always evaluates to [code]false[/code].
methods.name: matchn

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string begins with the given [param text]. See also [method ends_with].
methods.name: begins_with

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string ends with the given [param text]. See also [method begins_with].
methods.name: ends_with

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if all characters of this string can be found in [param text] in their original order. This is not the same as [method contains].
methods.name: is_subsequence_of

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if all characters of this string can be found in [param text] in their original order, [b]ignoring case[/b]. This is not the same as [method containsn].
methods.name: is_subsequence_ofn

methods.description: Returns an array containing the bigrams (pairs of consecutive characters) of this string.
methods.name: bigrams

methods.description: Returns the similarity index ([url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%B8rensen%E2%80%93Dice_coefficient]Sørensen-Dice coefficient[/url]) of this string compared to another. A result of [code]1.0[/code] means totally similar, while [code]0.0[/code] means totally dissimilar.
methods.name: similarity

methods.description: Formats the string by replacing all occurrences of [param placeholder] with the elements of [param values].
methods.name: format

methods.description: Replaces all occurrences of [param what] inside the string with the given [param forwhat].
methods.name: replace

methods.description: Replaces all [b]case-insensitive[/b] occurrences of [param what] inside the string with the given [param forwhat].
methods.name: replacen

methods.description: Replaces all occurrences of the Unicode character with code [param key] with the Unicode character with code [param with]. Faster version of [method replace] when the key is only one character long. To get a single character use [code]"X".unicode_at(0)[/code] (note that some strings, like compound letters and emoji, can be composed of multiple unicode codepoints, and will not work with this method, use [method length] to make sure).
methods.name: replace_char

methods.description: Replaces any occurrence of the characters in [param keys] with the Unicode character with code [param with]. See also [method replace_char].
methods.name: replace_chars

methods.description: Removes all occurrences of the Unicode character with code [param what]. Faster version of [method replace] when the key is only one character long and the replacement is [code]""[/code].
methods.name: remove_char

methods.description: Removes all occurrences of the characters in [param chars]. See also [method remove_char].
methods.name: remove_chars

methods.description: Repeats this string a number of times. [param count] needs to be greater than [code]0[/code]. Otherwise, returns an empty string.
methods.name: repeat

methods.description: Returns the copy of this string in reverse order. This operation works on unicode codepoints, rather than sequences of codepoints, and may break things like compound letters or emojis.
methods.name: reverse

methods.description: Inserts [param what] at the given [param position] in the string.
methods.name: insert

methods.description: Returns a string with [param chars] characters erased starting from [param position]. If [param chars] goes beyond the string's length given the specified [param position], fewer characters will be erased from the returned string. Returns an empty string if either [param position] or [param chars] is negative. Returns the original string unmodified if [param chars] is [code]0[/code].
methods.name: erase

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with changed appearance. Replaces underscores ([code]_[/code]) and hyphens ([code]-[/code]) with spaces, adds spaces before uppercase letters in the middle of a word, converts all letters to lowercase, then converts the first one and each one following a space to uppercase.
methods.name: capitalize

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]camelCase[/code].
methods.name: to_camel_case

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]PascalCase[/code].
methods.name: to_pascal_case

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]snake_case[/code].
methods.name: to_snake_case

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]kebab-case[/code].
methods.name: to_kebab_case

methods.description: Splits the string using a [param delimiter] and returns an array of the substrings. If [param delimiter] is an empty string, each substring will be a single character. This method is the opposite of [method join].
methods.name: split

methods.description: Splits the string using a [param delimiter] and returns an array of the substrings, starting from the end of the string. The splits in the returned array appear in the same order as the original string. If [param delimiter] is an empty string, each substring will be a single character.
methods.name: rsplit

methods.description: Splits the string into floats by using a [param delimiter] and returns a [PackedFloat64Array].
methods.name: split_floats

methods.description: Returns the concatenation of [param parts]' elements, with each element separated by the string calling this method. This method is the opposite of [method split].
methods.name: join

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]UPPERCASE[/code].
methods.name: to_upper

methods.description: Returns the string converted to [code]lowercase[/code].
methods.name: to_lower

methods.description: Returns the first [param length] characters from the beginning of the string. If [param length] is negative, strips the last [param length] characters from the string's end.
methods.name: left

methods.description: Returns the last [param length] characters from the end of the string. If [param length] is negative, strips the first [param length] characters from the string's beginning.
methods.name: right

methods.description: Strips all non-printable characters from the beginning and the end of the string. These include spaces, tabulations ([code]\t[/code]), and newlines ([code]\n[/code] [code]\r[/code]).
methods.name: strip_edges

methods.description: Strips all escape characters from the string. These include all non-printable control characters of the first page of the ASCII table (values from 0 to 31), such as tabulation ([code]\t[/code]) and newline ([code]\n[/code], [code]\r[/code]) characters, but [i]not[/i] spaces.
methods.name: strip_escapes

methods.description: Removes a set of characters defined in [param chars] from the string's beginning. See also [method rstrip].
methods.name: lstrip

methods.description: Removes a set of characters defined in [param chars] from the string's end. See also [method lstrip].
methods.name: rstrip

methods.description: If the string is a valid file name or path, returns the file extension without the leading period ([code].[/code]). Otherwise, returns an empty string.
methods.name: get_extension

methods.description: If the string is a valid file path, returns the full file path, without the extension.
methods.name: get_basename

methods.description: Concatenates [param path] at the end of the string as a subpath, adding [code]/[/code] if necessary.
methods.name: path_join

methods.description: Returns the character code at position [param at].
methods.name: unicode_at

methods.description: Indents every line of the string with the given [param prefix]. Empty lines are not indented. See also [method dedent] to remove indentation.
methods.name: indent

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with indentation (leading tabs and spaces) removed. See also [method indent] to add indentation.
methods.name: dedent

methods.description: Returns the 32-bit hash value representing the string's contents.
methods.name: hash

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5]MD5 hash[/url] of the string as another [String].
methods.name: md5_text

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1]SHA-1[/url] hash of the string as another [String].
methods.name: sha1_text

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2]SHA-256[/url] hash of the string as another [String].
methods.name: sha256_text

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MD5]MD5 hash[/url] of the string as a [PackedByteArray].
methods.name: md5_buffer

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-1]SHA-1[/url] hash of the string as a [PackedByteArray].
methods.name: sha1_buffer

methods.description: Returns the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-2]SHA-256[/url] hash of the string as a [PackedByteArray].
methods.name: sha256_buffer

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string's length is [code]0[/code] ([code]""[/code]). See also [method length].
methods.name: is_empty

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string contains [param what]. In GDScript, this corresponds to the [code]in[/code] operator.
methods.name: contains

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string contains [param what], [b]ignoring case[/b].
methods.name: containsn

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string is a path to a file or directory, and its starting point is explicitly defined. This method is the opposite of [method is_relative_path].
methods.name: is_absolute_path

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the string is a path, and its starting point is dependent on context. The path could begin from the current directory, or the current [Node] (if the string is derived from a [NodePath]), and may sometimes be prefixed with [code]"./"[/code]. This method is the opposite of [method is_absolute_path].
methods.name: is_relative_path

methods.description: If the string is a valid file path, converts the string into a canonical path. This is the shortest possible path, without [code]"./"[/code], and all the unnecessary [code]".."[/code] and [code]"/"[/code].
methods.name: simplify_path

methods.description: If the string is a valid file path, returns the base directory name.
methods.name: get_base_dir

methods.description: If the string is a valid file path, returns the file name, including the extension.
methods.name: get_file

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with special characters escaped using the XML standard. If [param escape_quotes] is [code]true[/code], the single quote ([code]'[/code]) and double quote ([code]"[/code]) characters are also escaped.
methods.name: xml_escape

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with escaped characters replaced by their meanings according to the XML standard.
methods.name: xml_unescape

methods.description: Encodes the string to URL-friendly format. This method is meant to properly encode the parameters in a URL when sending an HTTP request. See also [method uri_decode].
methods.name: uri_encode

methods.description: Decodes the string from its URL-encoded format. This method is meant to properly decode the parameters in a URL when receiving an HTTP request. See also [method uri_encode].
methods.name: uri_decode

methods.description: Decodes the file path from its URL-encoded format. Unlike [method uri_decode] this method leaves [code]+[/code] as is.
methods.name: uri_file_decode

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with special characters escaped using the C language standard.
methods.name: c_escape

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with escaped characters replaced by their meanings. Supported escape sequences are [code]\'[/code], [code]\"[/code], [code]\\[/code], [code]\a[/code], [code]\b[/code], [code]\f[/code], [code]\n[/code], [code]\r[/code], [code]\t[/code], [code]\v[/code].
methods.name: c_unescape

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with special characters escaped using the JSON standard. Because it closely matches the C standard, it is possible to use [method c_unescape] to unescape the string, if necessary.
methods.name: json_escape

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with all characters that are not allowed in [member Node.name] ([code].[/code] [code]:[/code] [code]@[/code] [code]/[/code] [code]"[/code] [code]%[/code]) replaced with underscores.
methods.name: validate_node_name

methods.description: Returns a copy of the string with all characters that are not allowed in [method is_valid_filename] replaced with underscores.
methods.name: validate_filename

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid ASCII identifier. A valid ASCII identifier may contain only letters, digits, and underscores ([code]_[/code]), and the first character may not be a digit.
methods.name: is_valid_ascii_identifier

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid Unicode identifier.
methods.name: is_valid_unicode_identifier

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid identifier. A valid identifier may contain only letters, digits and underscores ([code]_[/code]), and the first character may not be a digit.
methods.name: is_valid_identifier

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string represents a valid integer. A valid integer only contains digits, and may be prefixed with a positive ([code]+[/code]) or negative ([code]-[/code]) sign. See also [method to_int].
methods.name: is_valid_int

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string represents a valid floating-point number. A valid float may contain only digits, one decimal point ([code].[/code]), and the exponent letter ([code]e[/code]). It may also be prefixed with a positive ([code]+[/code]) or negative ([code]-[/code]) sign. Any valid integer is also a valid float (see [method is_valid_int]). See also [method to_float].
methods.name: is_valid_float

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid hexadecimal number. A valid hexadecimal number only contains digits or letters [code]A[/code] to [code]F[/code] (either uppercase or lowercase), and may be prefixed with a positive ([code]+[/code]) or negative ([code]-[/code]) sign.
methods.name: is_valid_hex_number

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid color in hexadecimal HTML notation. The string must be a hexadecimal value (see [method is_valid_hex_number]) of either 3, 4, 6 or 8 digits, and may be prefixed by a hash sign ([code]#[/code]). Other HTML notations for colors, such as names or [code]hsl()[/code], are not considered valid. See also [method Color.html].
methods.name: is_valid_html_color

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string represents a well-formatted IPv4 or IPv6 address. This method considers [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reserved_IP_addresses]reserved IP addresses[/url] such as [code]"0.0.0.0"[/code] and [code]"ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff:ffff"[/code] as valid.
methods.name: is_valid_ip_address

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this string is a valid file name. A valid file name cannot be empty, begin or end with space characters, or contain characters that are not allowed ([code]:[/code] [code]/[/code] [code]\[/code] [code]?[/code] [code]*[/code] [code]"[/code] [code]|[/code] [code]%[/code] [code]<[/code] [code]>[/code]).
methods.name: is_valid_filename

methods.description: Converts the string representing an integer number into an [int]. This method removes any non-number character and stops at the first decimal point ([code].[/code]). See also [method is_valid_int].
methods.name: to_int

methods.description: Converts the string representing a decimal number into a [float]. This method stops on the first non-number character, except the first decimal point ([code].[/code]) and the exponent letter ([code]e[/code]). See also [method is_valid_float].
methods.name: to_float

methods.description: Converts the string representing a hexadecimal number into an [int]. The string may be optionally prefixed with [code]"0x"[/code], and an additional [code]-[/code] prefix for negative numbers.
methods.name: hex_to_int

methods.description: Converts the string representing a binary number into an [int]. The string may optionally be prefixed with [code]"0b"[/code], and an additional [code]-[/code] prefix for negative numbers.
methods.name: bin_to_int

methods.description: Formats the string to be at least [param min_length] long by adding [param character]s to the left of the string, if necessary. See also [method rpad].
methods.name: lpad

methods.description: Formats the string to be at least [param min_length] long, by adding [param character]s to the right of the string, if necessary. See also [method lpad].
methods.name: rpad

methods.description: Formats the string representing a number to have an exact number of [param digits] [i]after[/i] the decimal point.
methods.name: pad_decimals

methods.description: Formats the string representing a number to have an exact number of [param digits] [i]before[/i] the decimal point.
methods.name: pad_zeros

methods.description: Removes the given [param prefix] from the start of the string, or returns the string unchanged.
methods.name: trim_prefix

methods.description: Removes the given [param suffix] from the end of the string, or returns the string unchanged.
methods.name: trim_suffix

methods.description: Converts the string to an [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCII]ASCII[/url]/Latin-1 encoded [PackedByteArray]. This method is slightly faster than [method to_utf8_buffer], but replaces all unsupported characters with spaces. This is the inverse of [method PackedByteArray.get_string_from_ascii].
methods.name: to_ascii_buffer

methods.description: Converts the string to a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8]UTF-8[/url] encoded [PackedByteArray]. This method is slightly slower than [method to_ascii_buffer], but supports all UTF-8 characters. For most cases, prefer using this method. This is the inverse of [method PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf8].
methods.name: to_utf8_buffer

methods.description: Converts the string to a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-16]UTF-16[/url] encoded [PackedByteArray]. This is the inverse of [method PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf16].
methods.name: to_utf16_buffer

methods.description: Converts the string to a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-32]UTF-32[/url] encoded [PackedByteArray]. This is the inverse of [method PackedByteArray.get_string_from_utf32].
methods.name: to_utf32_buffer

methods.description: Converts the string to a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wide_character]wide character[/url] ([code]wchar_t[/code], UTF-16 on Windows, UTF-32 on other platforms) encoded [PackedByteArray]. This is the inverse of [method PackedByteArray.get_string_from_wchar].
methods.name: to_wchar_buffer

methods.description: Converts the string to system multibyte code page encoded [PackedByteArray]. If conversion fails, empty array is returned.
methods.name: to_multibyte_char_buffer

methods.description: Decodes a hexadecimal string as a [PackedByteArray].
methods.name: hex_decode

methods.description: Converts the given [param number] to a string representation, in scientific notation.
methods.name: num_scientific

methods.description: Converts a [float] to a string representation of a decimal number, with the number of decimal places specified in [param decimals].
methods.name: num

methods.description: Converts the given [param number] to a string representation, with the given [param base].
methods.name: num_int64

methods.description: Converts the given unsigned [int] to a string representation, with the given [param base].
methods.name: num_uint64

methods.description: Returns a single Unicode character from the integer [param code]. You may use [url=https://unicodelookup.com/]unicodelookup.com[/url] or [url=https://www.unicode.org/charts/]unicode.org[/url] as points of reference.
methods.name: chr

methods.description: Converts [param size] which represents a number of bytes into a human-readable form.
methods.name: humanize_size

classes.brief_description: A 3D physics body specialized for characters moved by script.
classes.description: [CharacterBody3D] is a specialized class for physics bodies that are meant to be user-controlled. They are not affected by physics at all, but they affect other physics bodies in their path. They are mainly used to provide high-level API to move objects with wall and slope detection ([method move_and_slide] method) in addition to the general collision detection provided by [method PhysicsBody3D.move_and_collide]. This makes it useful for highly configurable physics bodies that must move in specific ways and collide with the world, as is often the case with user-controlled characters.

values.description: Apply when notions of walls, ceiling and floor are relevant. In this mode the body motion will react to slopes (acceleration/slowdown). This mode is suitable for grounded games like platformers.
values.name: MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED

values.description: Apply when there is no notion of floor or ceiling. All collisions will be reported as [code]on_wall[/code]. In this mode, when you slide, the speed will always be constant. This mode is suitable for games without ground like space games.
values.name: MOTION_MODE_FLOATING

values.description: Add the last platform velocity to the [member velocity] when you leave a moving platform.
values.name: PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_ADD_VELOCITY

values.description: Add the last platform velocity to the [member velocity] when you leave a moving platform, but any downward motion is ignored. It's useful to keep full jump height even when the platform is moving down.
values.name: PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_ADD_UPWARD_VELOCITY

values.description: Do nothing when leaving a platform.
values.name: PLATFORM_ON_LEAVE_DO_NOTHING

methods.description: Moves the body based on [member velocity]. If the body collides with another, it will slide along the other body rather than stop immediately. If the other body is a [CharacterBody3D] or [RigidBody3D], it will also be affected by the motion of the other body. You can use this to make moving and rotating platforms, or to make nodes push other nodes.
methods.name: move_and_slide

methods.description: Allows to manually apply a snap to the floor regardless of the body's velocity. This function does nothing when [method is_on_floor] returns [code]true[/code].
methods.name: apply_floor_snap

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided with the floor on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "floor" or not.
methods.name: is_on_floor

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided only with the floor on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "floor" or not.
methods.name: is_on_floor_only

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided with the ceiling on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "ceiling" or not.
methods.name: is_on_ceiling

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided only with the ceiling on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "ceiling" or not.
methods.name: is_on_ceiling_only

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided with a wall on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "wall" or not.
methods.name: is_on_wall

methods.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the body collided only with a wall on the last call of [method move_and_slide]. Otherwise, returns [code]false[/code]. The [member up_direction] and [member floor_max_angle] are used to determine whether a surface is "wall" or not.
methods.name: is_on_wall_only

methods.description: Returns the collision normal of the floor at the last collision point. Only valid after calling [method move_and_slide] and when [method is_on_floor] returns [code]true[/code].
methods.name: get_floor_normal

methods.description: Returns the collision normal of the wall at the last collision point. Only valid after calling [method move_and_slide] and when [method is_on_wall] returns [code]true[/code].
methods.name: get_wall_normal

methods.description: Returns the last motion applied to the [CharacterBody3D] during the last call to [method move_and_slide]. The movement can be split into multiple motions when sliding occurs, and this method return the last one, which is useful to retrieve the current direction of the movement.
methods.name: get_last_motion

methods.description: Returns the travel (position delta) that occurred during the last call to [method move_and_slide].
methods.name: get_position_delta

methods.description: Returns the current real velocity since the last call to [method move_and_slide]. For example, when you climb a slope, you will move diagonally even though the velocity is horizontal. This method returns the diagonal movement, as opposed to [member velocity] which returns the requested velocity.
methods.name: get_real_velocity

methods.description: Returns the floor's collision angle at the last collision point according to [param up_direction], which is [constant Vector3.UP] by default. This value is always positive and only valid after calling [method move_and_slide] and when [method is_on_floor] returns [code]true[/code].
methods.name: get_floor_angle

methods.description: Returns the linear velocity of the platform at the last collision point. Only valid after calling [method move_and_slide].
methods.name: get_platform_velocity

methods.description: Returns the angular velocity of the platform at the last collision point. Only valid after calling [method move_and_slide].
methods.name: get_platform_angular_velocity

methods.description: Returns the number of times the body collided and changed direction during the last call to [method move_and_slide].
methods.name: get_slide_collision_count

methods.description: Returns a [KinematicCollision3D], which contains information about a collision that occurred during the last call to [method move_and_slide]. Since the body can collide several times in a single call to [method move_and_slide], you must specify the index of the collision in the range 0 to ([method get_slide_collision_count] - 1). See also [method get_last_slide_collision].
methods.name: get_slide_collision

methods.description: Returns a [KinematicCollision3D] if a collision occurred. The returned value contains information about the latest collision that occurred during the last call to [method move_and_slide]. Returns [code]null[/code] if no collision occurred. See also [method get_slide_collision].
methods.name: get_last_slide_collision

properties.description: If [code]true[/code], the body will be able to move on the floor only. This option avoids to be able to walk on walls, it will however allow to slide down along them.

properties.description: Maximum angle (in radians) where a slope is still considered a floor (or a ceiling), rather than a wall, when calling [method move_and_slide]. The default value equals 45 degrees.

properties.description: Sets a snapping distance. When set to a value different from [code]0.0[/code], the body is kept attached to slopes when calling [method move_and_slide]. The snapping vector is determined by the given distance along the opposite direction of the [member up_direction].

properties.description: Sets the behavior to apply when you leave a moving platform. By default, to be physically accurate, when you leave the last platform velocity is applied.

properties.description: Collision layers that will be included for detecting floor bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the [CharacterBody3D]. By default, all floor bodies are detected and propagate their velocity.

properties.description: Collision layers that will be included for detecting wall bodies that will act as moving platforms to be followed by the [CharacterBody3D]. By default, all wall bodies are ignored.

properties.description: Extra margin used for collision recovery when calling [method move_and_slide].
properties.name: safe_margin

signals.description: Emitted when the mouse pointer enters any of this object's shapes. Requires [member input_ray_pickable] to be [code]true[/code] and at least one [member collision_layer] bit to be set.
